record.original_question: For Boolean-ring based methods for resolution-like first-order theorem proving, can more restrictive strategies be found, such as strategies using only single overlaps or only unifications of maximal atoms, while preserving completeness?

evidence.quote: Find more restrictive strategies in Boolean-ring based methods for resolution-like first-order theorem proving.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background. In Boolean-ring based theorem proving, first-order clauses are translated into polynomials over the Boolean ring GF(2)[X]/(x^2 − x : x ∈ X), where conjunction is multiplication, exclusive-or is addition, and atoms become indeterminates. Refutational theorem proving is then carried out by superposition-style inferences on these polynomials: given two polynomials P and Q sharing a (unifiable) atom A, one forms new polynomials by overlapping P and Q on A (after applying a most general unifier), and the goal is to derive the polynomial 1 (representing falsity). Standard completeness proofs allow "multiple overlaps" (superposing on several atoms simultaneously or considering many atom pairs) and impose only mild restrictions on which atoms may be selected.

Problem. Determine whether the following more restrictive inference strategies for Boolean-ring based resolution-like first-order theorem proving are refutationally complete:

(a) A "single-overlap" strategy, in which each inference between two polynomials P and Q is required to superpose on exactly one chosen atom (no simultaneous multi-atom overlap is permitted).

(b) A "maximal-atom unification" strategy, in which, with respect to a fixed admissible ordering on atoms, inferences are restricted to unifications of maximal atoms of the participating polynomials only.

In each case, prove completeness (every unsatisfiable set of clauses admits a derivation of 1 under the restricted strategy) or exhibit a counterexample showing incompleteness. More generally, identify and prove complete the most restrictive natural strategies of these types for Boolean-ring based first-order theorem proving.
artifact.status_search_result: Partial progress exists: a method restricting superposition to maximal atoms (extending Hsiang's N-strategy) with a completeness proof via semantic trees has been published, and a linear strategy plus O-linear/pseudo-O-linear strategies based on a partial ordering of atoms have been shown complete. Results on the unnecessity of multiple overlaps in completion theorem proving also exist. However, a definitive resolution of the general question of identifying the most restrictive complete strategies (single-overlap and maximal-atom unification combined) in the Boolean-ring setting does not appear to be fully settled in the literature found.

status_evidence.title: A New Method for the Boolean Ring Based Theorem Proving
status_evidence.snippet: Extends Hsiang's N-Strategy by considering only maximal atoms in an N-rule; completeness proved via semantic trees.
status_evidence.claim: Maximal-atom-restricted strategy proved complete in a Boolean-ring setting.

status_evidence.title: Linear strategy for boolean ring based theorem proving
status_evidence.snippet: Two inference rules with a linear strategy are both shown complete; partial ordering on atoms yields O-linear and pseudo-O-linear strategies.
status_evidence.claim: Further restrictive complete strategies have been established.

status_evidence.title: On The Unnecessity of Multiple Overlaps in Completion Theorem Proving
status_evidence.snippet: Shows multiple overlaps are unnecessary in completion theorem proving.
status_evidence.claim: Supports single-overlap sufficiency in related completion-style setting.
